strokes.text: obs-websocket cannot create a group or place a source directly inside one.
The provider does both through the native bridge, a small OBS plugin that ships in the provider repository.
What the Bridge Does
The bridge adds group requests to obs-websocket as vendor requests under the vendor name `obstf`.
The provider checks the version and capabilities of the bridge before every group write.
After each request the bridge verifies the result inside OBS, and the provider accepts only a verified outcome.
Requirements
OBS Studio 32.2.2 with obs-websocket 5.7.4, because the group resources refuse any other version.
A base canvas of 1920x1080.
A scene collection in absolute coordinate mode, which is what @resources/collection_seed creates.
macOS on Apple silicon, the only platform the bridge is built for today.
Groups are not available on Windows or Linux yet; scenes, sources, filters and placements outside groups do not need the bridge.
Installing the Bridge
Build the plugin from the provider repository:
git clone https://github.com/DigiBugCat/terraform-provider-obs
make -C terraform-provider-obs/native-bridge build
Install the built bundle while OBS is closed, either by copying it into the OBS plugin folder or with @resources/plugin and a manifest that pins it.
Start OBS afterwards, because a plugin is loaded only at startup.
Choosing Group Resources
@resources/group with @resources/group_source or @resources/group_input gives every child its own resource and its own line in the plan.
@resources/group_graph manages a group and its image children as one unit and repairs the group as a whole.
Pick one model for each group and do not mix them.
Existing Sources in a Group
@resources/scene_item with `parent_kind` set to `group` places a source that already exists into a group.
@resources/scene_contents with the same setting declares the complete contents of a group.
Coordinates
Positions of group children are measured from the top-left corner of the group, not of the canvas.
The group reports its own size in `observed_group_width` and `observed_group_height`.
